# 1.36.0: Rosa answers again, the agent can use the mouse, the chat gets things done

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are. Nothing changes in
how the agent works with program windows until you turn the new switch on.

## The model you picked stays

- When the model you picked for a chat was overloaded or hit its rate limit, the program silently
  answered with a fallback model, usually the heavy one. A model you picked by hand is now never
  replaced: if it is overloaded, the reply says so, and you can try again or pick another one.
  Fallback models remain only for **Auto**, where the program picks the model anyway.
- The "thought for" label next to the reply time is gone.

## The chat and the agent get things done

- When the chat doesn't know something, or it may have changed, it now searches the web or asks
  the agent before answering, instead of telling you to check it yourself.
- Facts about this PC that a task needs, the chat now gets through the agent without asking you
  first, and it no longer says it can't do something on this PC that the agent can.
- When an answer leads to something you would obviously want done on this PC next, the chat offers
  to do it.
- A short, informal or misspelled request is read by its most likely meaning, not answered with a
  list of questions.
- The agent carries your task to the end. It no longer refuses or argues over a task because of
  its own opinion of the task, its sources or its content, and finds out what it doesn't know with
  its tools. The program's own limits stay: it follows every refusal of the app and never works
  around it.
- These rules also reach chat and agent prompts you saved yourself.

## The chat talks with the agent

- An agent's report is no longer its last word. The chat can write back to it: ask what is
  unclear, point out a mistake, share what it found or give it the next part of the task. The
  agent keeps everything it did and learned, so the chat no longer starts a new agent from
  scratch to correct the old one.
- The agent stays available until the chat finishes its answer. Your own **Stop** and "faster"
  still reach the same agent while it works.

## Refusals go up a ladder of models

- A model now refuses only with a dedicated call, never in plain text. When the chat model
  refuses, its reply is dropped and a stronger model takes the task: the heavy chat model, then
  the new bypass model. A model you picked by hand goes the same way. You see a refusal only when
  no stronger model is left, as "I, model, refuse to carry out this task for these reasons: ...".
- When the agent refuses, the chat sees its reasons and either talks it over with the agent or
  gives the agent's task to a stronger model: fast and light go to heavy, heavy goes to bypass.
  The stronger model carries on from where the agent stopped, without seeing the refusal.
- The new **Bypass** section in **Settings → Models** sets that last model. It is Grok 4.7 out of
  the box.

## No more freezes on code blocks

- The program could freeze for good while an answer with a JSON code block was being written:
  the highlighting rule for an unfinished string tried more combinations with every character. A
  finished answer with a long string in a JSON list could freeze it too, when the chat was opened.
- The same flaw was in comments of C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C++, PHP and CSS, in XML and
  HTML comments and tag attributes, in F# and Koka strings, Haskell comments and nested blocks in
  Markdown. All of it is fixed, and ordinary code is highlighted exactly as before.

## Rosa no longer goes silent

- When his model answered with plain text instead of the expected format, Rosa's mind stopped,
  and he did not answer anything until the program was restarted. A plain-text answer in a talk
  is now taken as his reply; anywhere else it is ignored, and one failed request no longer
  silences him.
- A request to his model now gives up after 45 seconds instead of five minutes, so one slow
  answer no longer holds back the talk behind it. When a request fails, he says his words ran
  away.
- When his model only wanted to do something (cuddle, play) without saying a word, the talk
  counted as failed. Now he is asked once more for the words.
- **Talk** in his menu did nothing while he walked around or played. Now he stops and listens.
- His words no longer contradict what he does. His model used to be offered every action he
  knows, while Rosa silently skipped most of them (in the chat almost all of them), so he wrote
  "I'm lying down" and kept sitting. Now his model is offered only what he can actually do at that
  moment, one action per answer, and is told not to describe anything else. In the chat he can now
  lie down, nap and cuddle on the spot; he still doesn't walk away from the panel.
- With **Auto** in the Rosa slot and no Venice key he never answered. Auto now takes the default
  model of your key's provider.

## Rosa answers in his mood

His model now sees his day: how you treated him today (pets, treats, games, nose boops, tail
pulls, throws), what he did himself (bites, refusals to come, mischief), how much annoyance and
joy the day brought, how offended and how tired he is. His tone follows it. Offended, or annoyed
by you today, he answers prickly and short, but without rude words; pleased, he is warm; tired,
he is sleepy. His reactions to your chat messages follow the same mood. Your words are sent
exactly as before; the day is sent as numbers.

## Rosa's friendship is earned

Before, one action repeated over and over (booping his nose, a soft landing, praise, a kind talk)
raised his friendship without end.

- Friendship grows by at most 6 a day and falls by at most 18 a day, however often you repeat
  something. **Our friendship** says when it won't grow any more today.
- A wrong (pulling his tail, shaking him, a hard throw, rudeness, forgetting him for days) now
  weighs twice as much, and he remembers it. While he remembers, kindness warms him less. Hours
  don't make him forget; each kind day with attention and no wrongs erases part of it. Being kind
  from the start pays off. His model knows he remembers, and **Our friendship** shows it.
- Offended or cold, he may refuse to talk: **Talk** and **Chat** then don't open, and he turns
  away. He may also refuse to be held: he bites your hand and breaks free. Shaking him when he is
  angry always ends that way.
- With **Mischief** on, his bite knocks the mouse cursor aside. Turn **Mischief** off and he
  only bites.

## Games

- **End the game** in Rosa's menu stops any game early: laser, tag, hide and seek, ball, or a
  game he started himself. **Esc** works as before.
- Rosa can now catch the laser dot. Before, he only ran along his edge and hopped in place. A dot
  that touches him is caught; a dot just above him he jumps for. Keep it moving if you don't want
  him to win.
- In tag, pressing on him now catches him. Before, catching a running fox turned into picking him
  up, and the game silently ended.

## Chat with Rosa

**Chat** in Rosa's menu opens a small panel right above him with your past talks and a field to
write to him. It does not cover or block the program: you keep working while it is open, it moves
with Rosa, and **Esc** or the cross closes it. His replies appear in the panel. He now remembers up to 50 talks
instead of 12; his model still sees only the last six. The talks live in his memory file, so the
data archive, encryption and **Delete all data** cover them as before.

## Two new dark themes

- **Onyx**: a blue-tinted near-black, with thin cool borders and a silver-blue accent.
- **Carbon**: neutral graphite in the style of the ChatGPT desktop app: a darker sidebar, soft
  grey buttons and menus, and a white main button.

Both are in **Settings → Appearance → Theme**.

## Interface

- Interface scale has two new steps: 115% and 120%.
- The accent focus frame no longer appears around whole areas (the settings navigation, lists,
  panels) after a key press. It stays on buttons, switches, drop-downs and sliders, where it shows
  where Tab went.

## Work in program windows

- The agent can now operate the windows of this computer: program windows, the browser and
  Windows settings. It does so only when its own tools can't reach the goal or you asked for the
  work to be done in a program's window.
- Turn it on in **Settings → Security → Operating this PC**. It is off by default: while the agent
  works, screenshots and window text go to the provider of the agent's model.
- The agent does the clicking itself, with everything it already knows about the task. It reads
  the window's controls, looks at the screen when it needs to and does a few predictable steps at
  once, then checks the result. With the mouse it has up to 100 steps per task. Window work goes
  to a model that can see pictures; a model that can't works from the window's controls alone.
- Ask to be shown how to do something, and the agent highlights each place on the screen while
  you click yourself; **Done** on the panel moves it to the next step.

## While the agent holds the mouse

- The edges of all your screens glow in the theme's accent color, over the taskbar too, and the
  pointer turns into the soft pink Amarin pointer. Both go away when the work ends, and the
  pointer comes back even if the program closes unexpectedly.
- The program folds into a small panel at the edge of the screen: the current step and **Stop**.
  **Stop** stops the agent the same way stopping it from the chat does.
- When a click does need a question (with **Ask about everything**, or when the guard model could
  not check it), it is answered on the panel with **Yes** or **No**, so the window the agent works
  in keeps the focus. Other questions bring the program back for the answer and fold it again
  afterwards, returning the focus to the window the agent was working in.
- The panel and the glow never take the focus, are left out of the screenshots the agent sees,
  and never get in the way of a click.

## Limits

- The agent never clicks or types in this program's own windows, never types into a password
  field, a console, a terminal or the Run box, never types or pastes a command line anywhere and
  never presses the keys that delete files in File Explorer.
- Windows run as administrator, the sign-in screen and User Account Control prompts are refused,
  not worked around.
- Your request is your consent. In the normal access mode the agent clicks and types without
  asking you again. **Ask about everything** still asks before each step, and **Read only** allows
  none.

## The guard model judges by your request

- The guard model now checks each step against what you asked for in your own words, including
  your previous messages and the question you answered, so a short "yes, send it" is understood.
  It also sees what was already done in the task, what is on the screen and which button is about
  to be pressed.
- What carries out your request and doesn't go against it passes, including sending what you
  asked to send. It stops what you didn't ask for, data leaving the computer without your words
  asking for it, harm beyond the request and code nobody can read. Not being sure is no longer a
  reason to stop.
- A round of reads that don't leave the computer is no longer sent to the guard model, the same
  as in the chat, so the agent works faster.
- A task for later remembers your words from when it was set, sealed together with the task, so
  it runs at night the way you asked without stopping on questions you already answered. A task
  changed by hand or brought in from an archive loses this.

## Without you at the computer

- A task for later can use the mouse; it starts after a 10-second countdown on the panel that
  you can cancel. The screen is kept on while the agent works.
- When the agent of a task for later doesn't finish, the chat can now call it again and check
  the result itself. Before, it could only write a report, and promised a retry it couldn't start.
- A scheduled task can be allowed to use the mouse with its own switch, **May operate this PC**.
  Only the mouse may change anything in such a run; every other tool still only reads. The
  switch is sealed like commands for later and never comes in from an archive.

## Also

- An agent prompt saved unchanged from an earlier version is replaced by the new one, which no
  longer says the agent can't use the Windows interface.
- If Windows is locked when a task needs the mouse, the report says so plainly.
- Work in program windows, now or for later, always goes to the agent. A PowerShell script that
  brings a window forward or presses keys in it is refused: from the background it can't reach the
  window, and it used to report success anyway. Volume and media keys still work from a script.
- With **Operating this PC** off, the chat says the switch is needed instead of trying a script.

## Rolling back

Rolling back to 1.35 keeps your settings. A 115% or 120% scale becomes 100% there, and Onyx or
Carbon shows as the plain dark or light theme; coming back to 1.36 brings your choice back. Rosa
keeps his friendship on 1.35, but forgets the wrongs he remembered. 1.35 doesn't know the bypass
model: once it saves your settings, the bypass model is Grok 4.7 again when you come back.
